archetype.name: Point Guard (Shanahan timing distributor)
archetype.definition: An on-schedule distributor who wins by getting the ball out on time to Kittle, McCaffrey and whoever is open in a play-action system, then uses his legs to extend plays when the structure breaks.

report.headline: Top-six efficiency built early; the receiver-depleted slide since Week 5 matters more.
report.take:
Purdy is having the kind of season his system and his history say he should. He is sixth in EPA per dropback at 0.29, second in passing touchdowns, and third in sack rate. That is a quarterback a quarter of a point per dropback better than the league average and about a yard and a half better per dropback. It isn't a one-year spike. His 2023 led the league in EPA per play, and 2025 was sixth. The profile is familiar: very accurate underneath (78.7% on throws of 0-9 air yards, +7 CPOE), dangerous on the intermediate throws Shanahan's play-action creates (0.493 EPA on 10-19 yards), and a lot of production funneled through Kittle and a big-play outside receiver.

The season splits into two halves, though. Weeks 2 and 3 against Miami and Arizona, both bottom-six defenses by today's rankings, produced 23.3 and 22.9 EPA and carry a lot of the season total. Over the last three games his EPA per dropback has fallen to 0.035, about league average. In that stretch his sack rate doubled to 6.7% and his interception rate rose to 3.1%. Seattle (No. 2 defense) explains part of it, since it pressured him on 35.3% of dropbacks. Washington, a No. 25 defense, held him to 3.7 EPA, though, and the loss at Atlanta came with two interceptions. The better explanation is the receiver room. Mike Evans has been the most valuable target in the offense by a wide margin: 1.023 EPA per target and 40.9 EPA total, more than double Kittle. Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson are all now out or on IR. Throws to a 0.034-EPA-per-target McCaffrey are no substitute.

The numbers also flatter him in two places. In the red zone he has 11 touchdowns, no interceptions and an 18.8 CPOE. His 7.1% touchdown rate sits 2.6 points above the league. Both will cool. The 18 deep attempts at 0.902 EPA are a hint, not a trait. On the other side, the pocket work looks real. His pressure-to-sack rate has dropped from 35.5% as a rookie to 16.1% now, matching last year's 16.7%. His 15 scrambles have been worth 0.909 EPA apiece. Holding the ball 3.0 seconds is the cost of that creation, and he is being paid for it.

From here the outlook depends on health more than on Purdy. The bye lands at the right time: Evans is expected back, and Samuel, Robinson and McCaffrey are all aiming for the Raiders game. With them, the Weeks 1-4 version, roughly a top-eight passer, is the honest baseline. Without them, the last three weeks are the floor: efficient enough to win, not to carry.

strengths.title: Short-area accuracy that drives the offense
strengths.body: Nearly two-thirds of his charted throws are under 10 air yards. He completes 78.7% of the 0-9 range at +7 CPOE and a 63.8% success rate. This is the foundation of a Shanahan offense, and it held up through the recent slump. His CPOE over the last three games is still 4.4. It's a skill he has shown every season since 2023, so it should last.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance and scramble value
strengths.body: He turns only 16.1% of pressures into sacks, fourth-best, and gets pressured on just 14.4% of dropbacks. His 15 scrambles average 0.909 EPA with nine first downs. As a rookie he took sacks on 35.5% of pressures. Last season's 16.7% shows the improvement is a real change in how he handles a collapsing pocket, not noise.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle of the field
strengths.body: Play-action and crossers open the 10-19 yard window, and he has produced 0.493 EPA a throw there. Throws to the middle run at 0.581 EPA. This is where Evans and Kittle did their damage, so it depends on getting Evans back. Kittle's 0.349 EPA per target keeps a solid floor in place regardless.

concerns.title: Three-week drop to league average
concerns.body: His EPA per dropback over Weeks 5-7 is 0.035, down 0.255 from his season mark, and he averaged just 1.2 EPA a game. Sacks and interceptions both climbed. Seattle's pressure accounts for one game, but Washington and Atlanta were not imposing defenses. Most of it lines up with Evans and Samuel leaving the lineup, so it should ease if they return. If they don't, it could stick.

concerns.title: Red-zone and TD rate will regress
concerns.body: Eleven red-zone touchdowns with no picks and an 18.8 CPOE inside the 20 is not a repeatable rate. His 7.1% touchdown rate sits well above the league's 4.5%. His yardage is steady, but expect his touchdowns per game to settle closer to the 1.33 of the last three weeks than the 2.14 season mark.

concerns.title: Interception history and third downs
concerns.body: He has finished in the bottom fifth in interceptions in each of the last three seasons. This year's 1.9% rate is only mid-pack, and three picks in three games is a reminder. Third down is his weakest situation, at -5 CPOE and 0.073 EPA. That is where losing his best separators shows up first.

trend.note: He piled up EPA against weak defenses in Weeks 2-3. His per-game output then fell to a stretch of 2 to 4 EPA games as Seattle's pressure and a depleted receiver room caught up with him. The bye and expected returns give him a real chance to reverse it.

nextGame.headline: Rested, likely reloaded, against the league's worst short-pass defense
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas fits Purdy's game. The Raiders rank 32nd in EPA allowed on short passes and 23rd against the pass overall, and they give quarterbacks 20.1 PPR and 2.57 touchdowns a game, both bottom-five. They funnel an above-average share of targets to tight ends, which points straight at Kittle. The one real threat is their 4th-ranked hit rate. That is the same kind of heat that rattled him in Seattle, but his pressure-to-sack habits blunt it. They have held opposing WR1s under their averages, so Evans may not have a free day.

Availability decides how good this matchup is. Evans is expected back from his Achilles issue after the bye, and Samuel and Robinson each have a chance to return. McCaffrey's hamstring is described as mild, and the team expects him ready. If even Evans alone returns, the downfield and middle-of-field threat that drove the first month returns too. Stribling isn't due until December. On the Raiders' side, the injury list is mostly pass-catchers on their own offense. No line was posted at the time of the dossier.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game vs worst short defense
keyMatchups.body: Purdy's best area, the 0-9 yard window, meets the defense that bleeds the most there. Las Vegas allows 0.295 EPA on short passes, ranked last. Expect a high completion rate and lots of yards after the catch on schedule.

keyMatchups.title: Kittle against tight-end funnel
keyMatchups.body: Tight ends draw 29.5% of targets against Las Vegas, compared with 24% league-wide. Kittle has been the most-targeted 49er at 0.349 EPA a target. If the wideouts are slow to get back up to speed, Kittle is the steady outlet.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' pass rush hits
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas ranks 4th in hitting the quarterback, the one area where this defense can test him. His low pressure rate and 16.1% pressure-to-sack rate say he can absorb it, but Seattle showed what heavy pressure does to his efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Whether Evans is active and moving well. His return is the difference between the early-season Purdy and the last three weeks.

restOfSeason.body:
The skills underneath are stable: short accuracy, sack avoidance and scramble value have all held across two seasons. His yardage has stayed around 250 a game even through the slump. What won't hold is the touchdown efficiency, especially the perfect red-zone line. I'd expect him to settle into a high-floor, top-ten passer, around 240-275 yards and just under two touchdowns a game, assuming Evans and Samuel return.

Interceptions are the variable to watch. His career says turnovers creep up as aggressiveness rises, and this year's rate is already only middling. The 49ers' 2nd-ranked defense against the run keeps game scripts friendly, which limits the high-volume shootouts and also the ugly trailing ones.
swingFactors: Evans' Achilles holding up after the bye

confidence.note: Seven games, a clear recent dip, and receiver returns that are expected but not certain.
